definition: Computer vision dazzle, also known as CV dazzle, dazzle makeup, or anti-surveillance makeup, is a type of camouflage used to hamper facial recognition software.
details: However, the approach draws human attention and is readily spotted by human monitors.

explainer.lead: Computer vision dazzle is conspicuous makeup used as camouflage against facial-recognition software. It matters because confusing a camera system is not the same as going unnoticed: the look can draw human attention and be readily spotted by monitors.

tiers.eli5: It is like wearing a very bold costume for your face so a computer has more trouble recognizing you. The trick does not hide you from people: the unusual makeup can make them look at you even more.
tiers.practitioner: Treat CV dazzle as visible anti-recognition camouflage rather than a concealment technique. It is applied as facial makeup, and any evaluation must consider both software recognition and human observation. A design that hampers automated recognition may still attract immediate attention from monitors.
tiers.paperLevel: Computer vision dazzle is facial camouflage intended to hamper facial-recognition software observing the wearer. Its visibility creates a separate limitation for concealment: human observers can readily detect it and may have their attention drawn to it. Hampering recognition is not a guarantee of preventing identification.

explainer.example: A person wears CV dazzle makeup before walking past a camera running facial-recognition software. The makeup is meant to hamper automated recognition, but a security guard watching the feed can readily spot the person and their conspicuous appearance.

usedIn.name: Anti-surveillance
usedIn.detail: Worn as visible makeup intended to hamper facial-recognition software.

usedIn.name: Facial-recognition countermeasures
usedIn.detail: A camouflage approach that trades automated-recognition interference for high visibility to people.

explainer.intuition: The goal is to make a face harder for software to recognize, not to make the wearer blend into the surroundings. Its bold appearance can interfere with the machine while making the person more noticeable to humans.
howItWorks: The wearer applies visible dazzle makeup as facial camouflage.
A camera captures the altered appearance of the face.
Facial-recognition software processes that appearance, with the camouflage intended to hamper recognition.
A human monitor can still see the striking makeup and may notice the wearer more easily.
explainer.whyItMatters: CV dazzle highlights the difference between defeating automated recognition and avoiding observation. Its usefulness is limited by the attention it can attract from human monitors.
misconceptions: It does not make the wearer invisible or inconspicuous.
It targets facial-recognition software rather than human vision.
It is intended to hamper recognition, not guarantee anonymity.

diagram.caption: The same visible camouflage can hamper software while attracting human attention.
